us-al.name: ALABAMA
us-al.regulatory_agencies: Alabama Secretary of State (Elections Division) / Alabama Ethics Commission.
us-al.primary_statutes: Fair Campaign Practices Act (FCPA), Ala. Code § 17-5-1 et seq.; Alabama Ethics Act, Ala. Code § 36-25-1 et seq.

candidate_committee_registration.value: * Candidate must file Appointment of Principal Campaign Committee (PCC) within 5 days of qualifying or reaching **\$1,000** in contributions or expenditures (Ala. Code § 17-5-4).. * Candidate may act as sole committee/treasurer or appoint 2 to 5 members. Single checking account at an Alabama bank mandatory; petty cash transactions capped at \$100 (Ala. Code § 17-5-4, 17-5-5).. * Single authorized PCC per candidate; multi-office committees prohibited (Ala. Code § 17-5-4)..
candidate_committee_registration.official_source: Fair Campaign Practices Act (FCPA), Ala. Code § 17-5-1 et seq.; Alabama Ethics Act, Ala. Code § 36-25-1 et seq.

reporting_cadence_events.value: * Monthly reports; 4 weekly reports preceding election; daily reports during 8 days immediately preceding election if receiving/spending **\$5,000+**; major contributions of **\$20,000+** disclosed within 2 business days (Ala. Code § 17-5-8, 17-5-8.1).
reporting_cadence_events.official_source: Fair Campaign Practices Act (FCPA), Ala. Code § 17-5-1 et seq.; Alabama Ethics Act, Ala. Code § 36-25-1 et seq.

contribution_limits.value: Individuals: * **UNLIMITED (`NO_LIMIT`)** for statewide, legislative, and local offices (Ala. Code § 17-5-7).. PACs/Parties: * Unlimited contributions; PAC-to-PAC transfers strictly prohibited to prevent donor laundering (Ala. Code § 17-5-15(b))..
contribution_limits.official_source: Fair Campaign Practices Act (FCPA), Ala. Code § 17-5-1 et seq.; Alabama Ethics Act, Ala. Code § 36-25-1 et seq.

corporate_labor_treatment.value: Corporate & Union: * **UNLIMITED (`NO_LIMIT`)**; former \$500 cap repealed via Act 2013-311 (Ala. Code § 17-5-14.1).. Cash limit: * Maximum **\$100** cash contribution; anonymous contributions strictly banned (\$0) and escheat to state (Ala. Code § 17-5-7(c), 17-5-14).. Prohibited sources: * Foreign nationals (52 U.S.C. § 30121); straw donors (Ala. Code § 17-5-14); utilities regulated by PSC barred from giving to PSC candidates (Ala. Code § 17-5-15.1)..
corporate_labor_treatment.official_source: Fair Campaign Practices Act (FCPA), Ala. Code § 17-5-1 et seq.; Alabama Ethics Act, Ala. Code § 36-25-1 et seq.

public_financing.value: Not Applicable (`not-applicable`); no public financing system exists.
public_financing.official_source: Fair Campaign Practices Act (FCPA), Ala. Code § 17-5-1 et seq.; Alabama Ethics Act, Ala. Code § 36-25-1 et seq.

independent_expenditures.value: Registration required as PAC upon spending >\$1,000; daily 24-hr reporting during 8-day pre-election window for spending ≥\$5,000 (Ala. Code § 17-5-8(a)(3)). Paid-for disclaimer mandatory on all media (Ala. Code § 17-5-13).
independent_expenditures.official_source: Fair Campaign Practices Act (FCPA), Ala. Code § 17-5-1 et seq.; Alabama Ethics Act, Ala. Code § 36-25-1 et seq.

campaign_finance_enforcement_agency.value: Administered by Alabama Secretary of State (Elections Division) / Alabama Ethics Commission. under Fair Campaign Practices Act (FCPA), Ala. Code § 17-5-1 et seq.; Alabama Ethics Act, Ala. Code § 36-25-1 et seq..
campaign_finance_enforcement_agency.official_source: Fair Campaign Practices Act (FCPA), Ala. Code § 17-5-1 et seq.; Alabama Ethics Act, Ala. Code § 36-25-1 et seq.

late_failure_consequences.value: Statutory late fees per day/filing; compliance audit; disqualification from ballot/certificate of election for failure to file; civil penalty enforcement; criminal referral for willful violations. Official sanctions: Civil fines, Restitution, Class B felony referral.
late_failure_consequences.official_source: Fair Campaign Practices Act (FCPA), Ala. Code § 17-5-1 et seq.; Alabama Ethics Act, Ala. Code § 36-25-1 et seq.

financial_disclosure.value: Statement of Economic Interests (SEI) filed by April 30. * Statement of Economic Interests (SEI) filed annually by April 30 covering income >\$5,000, debts, and holdings (Ala. Code § 36-25-14).
financial_disclosure.official_source: Fair Campaign Practices Act (FCPA), Ala. Code § 17-5-1 et seq.; Alabama Ethics Act, Ala. Code § 36-25-1 et seq.

gift_restrictions.value: * Lobbyists capped at **\$25 per meal / \$150 annual aggregate** per official; principals capped at **\$50 per meal / \$250 annual aggregate** (Ala. Code § 36-25-7). De minimis threshold: \$25.
gift_restrictions.official_source: Fair Campaign Practices Act (FCPA), Ala. Code § 17-5-1 et seq.; Alabama Ethics Act, Ala. Code § 36-25-1 et seq.

conflicts_of_interest.value: * Mandatory recusal on matters of personal financial gain (Ala. Code § 36-25-5, 36-25-9).
conflicts_of_interest.official_source: Fair Campaign Practices Act (FCPA), Ala. Code § 17-5-1 et seq.; Alabama Ethics Act, Ala. Code § 36-25-1 et seq.

recusal_disqualification.value: Mandatory recusal: public officials must disclose conflicts on the official record and disqualify/abstain from voting, deliberating, or exercising official discretionary authority on matter affecting pecuniary interests. * Mandatory recusal on matters of personal financial gain (Ala. Code § 36-25-5, 36-25-9).
recusal_disqualification.official_source: Fair Campaign Practices Act (FCPA), Ala. Code § 17-5-1 et seq.; Alabama Ethics Act, Ala. Code § 36-25-1 et seq.

revolving_door_restrictions.value: * **2-year cooling-off period** for former legislators and constitutional officers from lobbying state government (Ala. Code § 36-25-13).
revolving_door_restrictions.official_source: Fair Campaign Practices Act (FCPA), Ala. Code § 17-5-1 et seq.; Alabama Ethics Act, Ala. Code § 36-25-1 et seq.

ethics_enforcement_structure.value: Ethics oversight and enforcement vested in Alabama Secretary of State (Elections Division) / Alabama Ethics Commission.. Authorized to investigate complaints, issue advisory opinions, conduct audits, issue subpoenas, levy civil fines, and refer criminal violations.
ethics_enforcement_structure.official_source: Fair Campaign Practices Act (FCPA), Ala. Code § 17-5-1 et seq.; Alabama Ethics Act, Ala. Code § 36-25-1 et seq.

lobbyist_registration_trigger.value: Administered by Alabama Ethics Commission. Trigger: any compensation or spending to influence official action. Fee: \$100. Quarterly expenditure reports due April 30, July 31, October 31, January 31 (Ala. Code § 36-25-18).
lobbyist_registration_trigger.official_source: Fair Campaign Practices Act (FCPA), Ala. Code § 17-5-1 et seq.; Alabama Ethics Act, Ala. Code § 36-25-1 et seq.

client_principal_relationship.value: Principals/clients employing lobbyists must file formal authorization/registration, certify expenditure reporting, and pay applicable principal fees alongside individual lobbyist registrations.
client_principal_relationship.official_source: Fair Campaign Practices Act (FCPA), Ala. Code § 17-5-1 et seq.; Alabama Ethics Act, Ala. Code § 36-25-1 et seq.

lobbying_reporting_scope_cadence.value: Reporting cadence: quarterly. Discloses all lobbying compensation, itemized expenses for meals, entertainment, travel, gifts, advertising, and specific legislative/administrative bill or issue tracking.
lobbying_reporting_scope_cadence.official_source: Fair Campaign Practices Act (FCPA), Ala. Code § 17-5-1 et seq.; Alabama Ethics Act, Ala. Code § 36-25-1 et seq.

lobbying_gift_restrictions.value: Lobbyist gift rule: $25 meal / $150 annual aggregate. Prohibits gifts, gratuities, entertainment, or meals from registered lobbyists/principals exceeding statutory cap. Sessional fundraising bans apply in applicable legislative cycles.
lobbying_gift_restrictions.official_source: Fair Campaign Practices Act (FCPA), Ala. Code § 17-5-1 et seq.; Alabama Ethics Act, Ala. Code § 36-25-1 et seq.

lobbying_enforcement_body.value: Lobbyist registry and compliance enforcement administered by Alabama Secretary of State (Elections Division) / Alabama Ethics Commission..
lobbying_enforcement_body.official_source: Fair Campaign Practices Act (FCPA), Ala. Code § 17-5-1 et seq.; Alabama Ethics Act, Ala. Code § 36-25-1 et seq.

lobbying_structural_exceptions.value: Statutory exceptions: private citizens expressing personal opinions without compensation, public employees acting in official capacity, news media in regular dissemination of news/editorial, and invited expert witnesses giving formal legislative testimony.
lobbying_structural_exceptions.official_source: Fair Campaign Practices Act (FCPA), Ala. Code § 17-5-1 et seq.; Alabama Ethics Act, Ala. Code § 36-25-1 et seq.

candidate_committee_registration.value: * Must file Letter of Intent / Registration prior to first dollar (\$0.01) raised or spent, and full registration within 15 days of becoming a candidate (AS 15.13.060; 2 AAC 50.282).. * Mandatory treasurer; candidate may serve as treasurer. Mandatory depository account in an Alaska-chartered bank (AS 15.13.060(b)).. * Single authorized committee per office (AS 15.13.060)..
candidate_committee_registration.official_source: AS 15.13 (Campaign Disclosure); AS 24.45 (Lobbying); AS 24.60 & AS 39.50 (Ethics).

reporting_cadence_events.value: * 30-day pre-election, 7-day pre-election, 105-day post-election; 24-hr flash report for contributions >\$250 received within 9 days of election (AS 15.13.110).
reporting_cadence_events.official_source: AS 15.13 (Campaign Disclosure); AS 24.45 (Lobbying); AS 24.60 & AS 39.50 (Ethics).

contribution_limits.value: Individuals: * **UNLIMITED (`NO_LIMIT`)** effective 2021–2026 under 9th Circuit *Thompson v. Hebdon* ruling striking down \$500 limit. (Pending: Ballot Measure 1 approved Aug 2026 restores **\$2,000 per cycle** limit effective late 2026).. PACs/Parties: * Unlimited under *Thompson v. Hebdon*..
contribution_limits.official_source: AS 15.13 (Campaign Disclosure); AS 24.45 (Lobbying); AS 24.60 & AS 39.50 (Ethics).

corporate_labor_treatment.value: Corporate & Union: * **PROHIBITED (\$0)** from treasury funds to candidates (AS 15.13.074(f)).. Cash limit: * Maximum **\$100** cash; anonymous contributions prohibited (\$0) (AS 15.13.074(b)).. Prohibited sources: * Foreign nationals; sole-source state contractors; straw donors..
corporate_labor_treatment.official_source: AS 15.13 (Campaign Disclosure); AS 24.45 (Lobbying); AS 24.60 & AS 39.50 (Ethics).

public_financing.official_source: AS 15.13 (Campaign Disclosure); AS 24.45 (Lobbying); AS 24.60 & AS 39.50 (Ethics).

independent_expenditures.value: Registration required >\$500; 24-hr report for expenditures >\$250 within 9 days of election (AS 15.13.135). Attribution must list **top 3 contributors** (AS 15.13.090).
independent_expenditures.official_source: AS 15.13 (Campaign Disclosure); AS 24.45 (Lobbying); AS 24.60 & AS 39.50 (Ethics).

campaign_finance_enforcement_agency.value: Administered by Alaska Public Offices Commission (APOC). under AS 15.13 (Campaign Disclosure); AS 24.45 (Lobbying); AS 24.60 & AS 39.50 (Ethics)..
campaign_finance_enforcement_agency.official_source: AS 15.13 (Campaign Disclosure); AS 24.45 (Lobbying); AS 24.60 & AS 39.50 (Ethics).

late_failure_consequences.value: Statutory late fees per day/filing; compliance audit; disqualification from ballot/certificate of election for failure to file; civil penalty enforcement; criminal referral for willful violations. Official sanctions: Civil fines up to $5,000, Removal from office, Misdemeanor referral.
late_failure_consequences.official_source: AS 15.13 (Campaign Disclosure); AS 24.45 (Lobbying); AS 24.60 & AS 39.50 (Ethics).

financial_disclosure.value: Public Official Financial Disclosure (POFD) filed by March 15. * Public Official Financial Disclosure (POFD) filed annually by March 15 (AS 39.50.020).
financial_disclosure.official_source: AS 15.13 (Campaign Disclosure); AS 24.45 (Lobbying); AS 24.60 & AS 39.50 (Ethics).

gift_restrictions.value: * **STRICT ZERO-GIFT BAN** on gifts from lobbyists to legislators (AS 24.60.080); non-lobbyist gifts >\$250 must be reported (AS 39.52.130).
gift_restrictions.official_source: AS 15.13 (Campaign Disclosure); AS 24.45 (Lobbying); AS 24.60 & AS 39.50 (Ethics).

conflicts_of_interest.value: * Mandatory declaration and recusal on matters of substantial financial interest (AS 24.60.030).
conflicts_of_interest.official_source: AS 15.13 (Campaign Disclosure); AS 24.45 (Lobbying); AS 24.60 & AS 39.50 (Ethics).

recusal_disqualification.value: Mandatory recusal: public officials must disclose conflicts on the official record and disqualify/abstain from voting, deliberating, or exercising official discretionary authority on matter affecting pecuniary interests. * Mandatory declaration and recusal on matters of substantial financial interest (AS 24.60.030).
recusal_disqualification.official_source: AS 15.13 (Campaign Disclosure); AS 24.45 (Lobbying); AS 24.60 & AS 39.50 (Ethics).

revolving_door_restrictions.value: * **1-year cooling-off period** for former legislators and executive commissioners (AS 24.60.035, 39.52.180).
revolving_door_restrictions.official_source: AS 15.13 (Campaign Disclosure); AS 24.45 (Lobbying); AS 24.60 & AS 39.50 (Ethics).

ethics_enforcement_structure.value: Ethics oversight and enforcement vested in Alaska Public Offices Commission (APOC).. Authorized to investigate complaints, issue advisory opinions, conduct audits, issue subpoenas, levy civil fines, and refer criminal violations.
ethics_enforcement_structure.official_source: AS 15.13 (Campaign Disclosure); AS 24.45 (Lobbying); AS 24.60 & AS 39.50 (Ethics).

lobbyist_registration_trigger.value: Administered by APOC. Trigger: earning or spending >\$250/quarter. Monthly reporting during legislative session, quarterly off-session (AS 24.45.041).
lobbyist_registration_trigger.official_source: AS 15.13 (Campaign Disclosure); AS 24.45 (Lobbying); AS 24.60 & AS 39.50 (Ethics).

client_principal_relationship.official_source: AS 15.13 (Campaign Disclosure); AS 24.45 (Lobbying); AS 24.60 & AS 39.50 (Ethics).

lobbying_reporting_scope_cadence.official_source: AS 15.13 (Campaign Disclosure); AS 24.45 (Lobbying); AS 24.60 & AS 39.50 (Ethics).

lobbying_gift_restrictions.official_source: AS 15.13 (Campaign Disclosure); AS 24.45 (Lobbying); AS 24.60 & AS 39.50 (Ethics).

lobbying_enforcement_body.value: Lobbyist registry and compliance enforcement administered by Alaska Public Offices Commission (APOC)..
lobbying_enforcement_body.official_source: AS 15.13 (Campaign Disclosure); AS 24.45 (Lobbying); AS 24.60 & AS 39.50 (Ethics).

lobbying_structural_exceptions.official_source: AS 15.13 (Campaign Disclosure); AS 24.45 (Lobbying); AS 24.60 & AS 39.50 (Ethics).

us-az.name: ARIZONA
us-az.regulatory_agencies: Arizona Secretary of State / Citizens Clean Elections Commission (CCEC).
us-az.primary_statutes: A.R.S. Title 16, Chapter 6 (A.R.S. § 16-901 et seq.); Clean Elections Act, A.R.S. § 16-940 et seq.

candidate_committee_registration.value: * Mandatory committee registration within 10 days of reaching **\$1,500** in contributions/expenditures for Statewide/Legislative/County, or **\$500** for City/Town (A.R.S. § 16-905).. * Mandatory treasurer; candidate may serve as treasurer; single dedicated campaign bank account (A.R.S. § 16-906).. * Single candidate committee per office sought (A.R.S. § 16-905)..
candidate_committee_registration.official_source: A.R.S. Title 16, Chapter 6 (A.R.S. § 16-901 et seq.); Clean Elections Act, A.R.S. § 16-940 et seq.

reporting_cadence_events.value: * Quarterly reports; pre-election report 10 days before election; post-election report 15 days after (A.R.S. § 16-927).
reporting_cadence_events.official_source: A.R.S. Title 16, Chapter 6 (A.R.S. § 16-901 et seq.); Clean Elections Act, A.R.S. § 16-940 et seq.

contribution_limits.value: Individuals: * **\$5,500** per cycle for Statewide and Legislative candidates; **\$6,750** for Local (A.R.S. § 16-912).. PACs/Parties: * Standard PAC: \$5,500; Mega PAC (>500 members): \$11,000. Political party to candidate: \$110,000 (Statewide) / \$11,000 (Leg) (A.R.S. § 16-914, 16-915)..
contribution_limits.official_source: A.R.S. Title 16, Chapter 6 (A.R.S. § 16-901 et seq.); Clean Elections Act, A.R.S. § 16-940 et seq.

corporate_labor_treatment.value: Corporate & Union: * **PROHIBITED (\$0)** from treasury funds directly to candidates (Ariz. Const. art. XIV, § 18; A.R.S. § 16-916).. Cash limit: * Maximum **\$100** cash; anonymous contributions prohibited (\$0) (A.R.S. § 16-907).. Prohibited sources: * Foreign nationals; corporations/unions directly; straw donors (A.R.S. § 16-916, 16-917)..
corporate_labor_treatment.official_source: A.R.S. Title 16, Chapter 6 (A.R.S. § 16-901 et seq.); Clean Elections Act, A.R.S. § 16-940 et seq.

public_financing.value: **ACTIVE STATEWIDE FULL PUBLIC FINANCING** (Citizens Clean Elections Act). Candidates collect \$5 qualifying contributions (1,500 for Governor, 200 for Legislature) to unlock full public grants for primary and general campaigns (A.R.S. § 16-940 et seq.).
public_financing.official_source: A.R.S. Title 16, Chapter 6 (A.R.S. § 16-901 et seq.); Clean Elections Act, A.R.S. § 16-940 et seq.

independent_expenditures.value: Registration trigger: >\$1,000. 24-hr report for expenditures >\$1,000 within 20 days of election (A.R.S. § 16-958). **Voters' Right to Know Act (Prop 211):** entities spending >\$50,000 statewide must disclose original source donors giving >\$5,000 (A.R.S. § 16-971 et seq.).
independent_expenditures.official_source: A.R.S. Title 16, Chapter 6 (A.R.S. § 16-901 et seq.); Clean Elections Act, A.R.S. § 16-940 et seq.

campaign_finance_enforcement_agency.value: Administered by Arizona Secretary of State / Citizens Clean Elections Commission (CCEC). under A.R.S. Title 16, Chapter 6 (A.R.S. § 16-901 et seq.); Clean Elections Act, A.R.S. § 16-940 et seq..
campaign_finance_enforcement_agency.official_source: A.R.S. Title 16, Chapter 6 (A.R.S. § 16-901 et seq.); Clean Elections Act, A.R.S. § 16-940 et seq.

late_failure_consequences.value: Statutory late fees per day/filing; compliance audit; disqualification from ballot/certificate of election for failure to file; civil penalty enforcement; criminal referral for willful violations. Official sanctions: Civil penalties up to $5,000, Class 6 felony / Class 1 misdemeanor referral.
late_failure_consequences.official_source: A.R.S. Title 16, Chapter 6 (A.R.S. § 16-901 et seq.); Clean Elections Act, A.R.S. § 16-940 et seq.

financial_disclosure.value: Statement of Financial Interest filed by January 31. * Annual Statement of Financial Interest filed by January 31 (A.R.S. § 38-541 et seq.).
financial_disclosure.official_source: A.R.S. Title 16, Chapter 6 (A.R.S. § 16-901 et seq.); Clean Elections Act, A.R.S. § 16-940 et seq.

gift_restrictions.value: * **STRICT ZERO-GIFT BAN** on gifts from lobbyists/principals to state officials (A.R.S. § 41-1232.08).
gift_restrictions.official_source: A.R.S. Title 16, Chapter 6 (A.R.S. § 16-901 et seq.); Clean Elections Act, A.R.S. § 16-940 et seq.

conflicts_of_interest.value: * Mandatory disclosure and abstention on matters of substantial personal interest (A.R.S. § 38-501 et seq.).
conflicts_of_interest.official_source: A.R.S. Title 16, Chapter 6 (A.R.S. § 16-901 et seq.); Clean Elections Act, A.R.S. § 16-940 et seq.

recusal_disqualification.value: Mandatory recusal: public officials must disclose conflicts on the official record and disqualify/abstain from voting, deliberating, or exercising official discretionary authority on matter affecting pecuniary interests. * Mandatory disclosure and abstention on matters of substantial personal interest (A.R.S. § 38-501 et seq.).
recusal_disqualification.official_source: A.R.S. Title 16, Chapter 6 (A.R.S. § 16-901 et seq.); Clean Elections Act, A.R.S. § 16-940 et seq.

revolving_door_restrictions.value: * **1-year cooling-off period** prohibiting former officials from representing clients before their former agency (A.R.S. § 38-504).
revolving_door_restrictions.official_source: A.R.S. Title 16, Chapter 6 (A.R.S. § 16-901 et seq.); Clean Elections Act, A.R.S. § 16-940 et seq.

ethics_enforcement_structure.value: Ethics oversight and enforcement vested in Arizona Secretary of State / Citizens Clean Elections Commission (CCEC).. Authorized to investigate complaints, issue advisory opinions, conduct audits, issue subpoenas, levy civil fines, and refer criminal violations.
ethics_enforcement_structure.official_source: A.R.S. Title 16, Chapter 6 (A.R.S. § 16-901 et seq.); Clean Elections Act, A.R.S. § 16-940 et seq.

lobbyist_registration_trigger.value: Regulated by Secretary of State. Trigger: compensated lobbying. Quarterly reports due Jan 31, Apr 30, Jul 31, Oct 31 (A.R.S. § 41-1232).
lobbyist_registration_trigger.official_source: A.R.S. Title 16, Chapter 6 (A.R.S. § 16-901 et seq.); Clean Elections Act, A.R.S. § 16-940 et seq.

client_principal_relationship.official_source: A.R.S. Title 16, Chapter 6 (A.R.S. § 16-901 et seq.); Clean Elections Act, A.R.S. § 16-940 et seq.

lobbying_reporting_scope_cadence.value: Reporting cadence: quarterly. Discloses all lobbying compensation, itemized expenses for meals, entertainment, travel, gifts, advertising, and specific legislative/administrative bill or issue tracking.
lobbying_reporting_scope_cadence.official_source: A.R.S. Title 16, Chapter 6 (A.R.S. § 16-901 et seq.); Clean Elections Act, A.R.S. § 16-940 et seq.

lobbying_gift_restrictions.value: Lobbyist gift rule: $0 (Strict lobbyist gift ban). Prohibits gifts, gratuities, entertainment, or meals from registered lobbyists/principals exceeding statutory cap. Sessional fundraising bans apply in applicable legislative cycles.
lobbying_gift_restrictions.official_source: A.R.S. Title 16, Chapter 6 (A.R.S. § 16-901 et seq.); Clean Elections Act, A.R.S. § 16-940 et seq.

lobbying_enforcement_body.official_source: A.R.S. Title 16, Chapter 6 (A.R.S. § 16-901 et seq.); Clean Elections Act, A.R.S. § 16-940 et seq.

us-ar.name: ARKANSAS
us-ar.primary_statutes: Ark. Code Ann. Title 7, Chapter 6; Title 21, Chapter 8; Constitutional Amendment 94.

candidate_committee_registration.value: * Candidate must file Statement of Organization within 15 days of receiving or spending **\$500** or qualifying for ballot (Ark. Code Ann. § 7-6-207).. * Candidate may act as treasurer; dedicated checking account in an Arkansas bank mandatory (Ark. Code Ann. § 7-6-203).. * Single candidate committee per office sought..
candidate_committee_registration.official_source: Ark. Code Ann. Title 7, Chapter 6; Title 21, Chapter 8; Constitutional Amendment 94.

reporting_cadence_events.value: * Monthly reports due 15 days after month-end; pre-election report 7 days before election; final report 30 days after election (Ark. Code Ann. § 7-6-207).
reporting_cadence_events.official_source: Ark. Code Ann. Title 7, Chapter 6; Title 21, Chapter 8; Constitutional Amendment 94.

contribution_limits.value: Individuals: * **\$3,500** per candidate per election (Primary, Runoff, and General separate; Ark. Code Ann. § 7-6-203(a)(1)).. PACs/Parties: * Approved PACs: \$3,500 per election. Political parties: \$3,500 per election..
contribution_limits.official_source: Ark. Code Ann. Title 7, Chapter 6; Title 21, Chapter 8; Constitutional Amendment 94.

corporate_labor_treatment.value: Corporate & Union: * **PROHIBITED (\$0)** from treasury funds under Constitutional Amendment 94.. Cash limit: * Maximum **\$100** cash; anonymous contributions capped at \$50 aggregate (Ark. Code Ann. § 7-6-203(a)(2)).. Prohibited sources: * Corporations/unions directly; foreign nationals; straw donors..
corporate_labor_treatment.official_source: Ark. Code Ann. Title 7, Chapter 6; Title 21, Chapter 8; Constitutional Amendment 94.

public_financing.official_source: Ark. Code Ann. Title 7, Chapter 6; Title 21, Chapter 8; Constitutional Amendment 94.

independent_expenditures.value: Reporting trigger: >\$500 aggregate per year. Quarterly reporting plus 7-day pre-election report (Ark. Code Ann. § 7-6-220). Paid-for disclaimer mandatory.
independent_expenditures.official_source: Ark. Code Ann. Title 7, Chapter 6; Title 21, Chapter 8; Constitutional Amendment 94.

campaign_finance_enforcement_agency.value: Administered by Arkansas Ethics Commission. under Ark. Code Ann. Title 7, Chapter 6; Title 21, Chapter 8; Constitutional Amendment 94..
campaign_finance_enforcement_agency.official_source: Ark. Code Ann. Title 7, Chapter 6; Title 21, Chapter 8; Constitutional Amendment 94.

late_failure_consequences.value: Statutory late fees per day/filing; compliance audit; disqualification from ballot/certificate of election for failure to file; civil penalty enforcement; criminal referral for willful violations. Official sanctions: Civil fines up to $2,000 per violation, Misdemeanor referral.
late_failure_consequences.official_source: Ark. Code Ann. Title 7, Chapter 6; Title 21, Chapter 8; Constitutional Amendment 94.

financial_disclosure.value: Statement of Financial Interest (SFI) filed by January 31. * Statement of Financial Interest (SFI) filed annually by January 31 (Ark. Code Ann. § 21-8-701).
financial_disclosure.official_source: Ark. Code Ann. Title 7, Chapter 6; Title 21, Chapter 8; Constitutional Amendment 94.

gift_restrictions.value: * **STRICT ZERO-GIFT BAN** under Amendment 94 ("not a cup of coffee rule") barring lobbyists and employers from giving gifts to statewide elected officials and legislators (Ark. Const. art. XIX, § 30).
gift_restrictions.official_source: Ark. Code Ann. Title 7, Chapter 6; Title 21, Chapter 8; Constitutional Amendment 94.

conflicts_of_interest.value: * Prohibited from using office for private financial gain; mandatory recusal on conflicts (Ark. Code Ann. § 21-8-304).
conflicts_of_interest.official_source: Ark. Code Ann. Title 7, Chapter 6; Title 21, Chapter 8; Constitutional Amendment 94.

recusal_disqualification.value: Mandatory recusal: public officials must disclose conflicts on the official record and disqualify/abstain from voting, deliberating, or exercising official discretionary authority on matter affecting pecuniary interests. * Prohibited from using office for private financial gain; mandatory recusal on conflicts (Ark. Code Ann. § 21-8-304).
recusal_disqualification.official_source: Ark. Code Ann. Title 7, Chapter 6; Title 21, Chapter 8; Constitutional Amendment 94.

revolving_door_restrictions.value: * **2-year cooling-off period** for former legislators from lobbying the General Assembly (Ark. Const. art. XIX, § 30).
revolving_door_restrictions.official_source: Ark. Code Ann. Title 7, Chapter 6; Title 21, Chapter 8; Constitutional Amendment 94.

ethics_enforcement_structure.value: Ethics oversight and enforcement vested in Arkansas Ethics Commission.. Authorized to investigate complaints, issue advisory opinions, conduct audits, issue subpoenas, levy civil fines, and refer criminal violations.
ethics_enforcement_structure.official_source: Ark. Code Ann. Title 7, Chapter 6; Title 21, Chapter 8; Constitutional Amendment 94.

lobbyist_registration_trigger.value: Regulated by Arkansas Ethics Commission. Trigger: earning or spending >\$400/quarter. Monthly reports during session, quarterly off-session (Ark. Code Ann. § 21-8-601).
lobbyist_registration_trigger.official_source: Ark. Code Ann. Title 7, Chapter 6; Title 21, Chapter 8; Constitutional Amendment 94.

client_principal_relationship.value: Principals/clients employing lobbyists must file formal authorization/registration, certify expenditure reporting, and pay applicable principal fees alongside individual lobbyist registrations.
client_principal_relationship.official_source: Ark. Code Ann. Title 7, Chapter 6; Title 21, Chapter 8; Constitutional Amendment 94.

lobbying_reporting_scope_cadence.value: Reporting cadence: monthly_in_session_quarterly_off. Discloses all lobbying compensation, itemized expenses for meals, entertainment, travel, gifts, advertising, and specific legislative/administrative bill or issue tracking.
lobbying_reporting_scope_cadence.official_source: Ark. Code Ann. Title 7, Chapter 6; Title 21, Chapter 8; Constitutional Amendment 94.

lobbying_gift_restrictions.value: Lobbyist gift rule: $0 (Strict zero-gift ban under Amendment 94). Prohibits gifts, gratuities, entertainment, or meals from registered lobbyists/principals exceeding statutory cap. Sessional fundraising bans apply in applicable legislative cycles.
lobbying_gift_restrictions.official_source: Ark. Code Ann. Title 7, Chapter 6; Title 21, Chapter 8; Constitutional Amendment 94.

lobbying_enforcement_body.value: Lobbyist registry and compliance enforcement administered by Arkansas Ethics Commission..

lobbying_structural_exceptions.value: Statutory exceptions: private citizens expressing personal opinions without compensation, public employees acting in official capacity, news media in regular dissemination of news/editorial, and invited expert witnesses giving formal legislative testimony.
lobbying_structural_exceptions.official_source: Ark. Code Ann. Title 7, Chapter 6; Title 21, Chapter 8; Constitutional Amendment 94.

us-ca.name: CALIFORNIA
us-ca.primary_statutes: Political Reform Act of 1974 (PRA), Cal. Gov. Code § 81000 et seq.; 2 CCR § 18110 et seq.

candidate_committee_registration.value: * Candidate must file Form 501 (Candidate Intention Statement) *prior to* soliciting or receiving any contribution. Candidate committee formed upon receiving/spending **\$2,000** in a calendar year (file Form 410 within 10 days; Cal. Gov. Code § 84101, 85200).. * Mandatory treasurer; candidate may serve as treasurer; single designated campaign depository account in an authorized financial institution in California (Cal. Gov. Code § 84100, 85201).. * Single candidate committee per specific elective office sought (Cal. Gov. Code § 85201)..
candidate_committee_registration.official_source: Political Reform Act of 1974 (PRA), Cal. Gov. Code § 81000 et seq.; 2 CCR § 18110 et seq.

reporting_cadence_events.value: * Semi-annual (Jan 31, July 31); two pre-election filings (40 days and 12 days before election). **90-Day Election Window 24-Hour Reporting:** Any contribution of **\$1,000 or more** received within 90 days before an election must be reported within **24 hours** (Form 497; Cal. Gov. Code § 84203).
reporting_cadence_events.official_source: Political Reform Act of 1974 (PRA), Cal. Gov. Code § 81000 et seq.; 2 CCR § 18110 et seq.

contribution_limits.value: Individuals: *. PACs/Parties: * Small Contributor Committees: double individual limit (\$78,400 Gov / \$11,800 Leg). Political Parties to Candidate: **UNLIMITED** contributions (Cal. Gov. Code § 85303)..
contribution_limits.official_source: Political Reform Act of 1974 (PRA), Cal. Gov. Code § 81000 et seq.; 2 CCR § 18110 et seq.

corporate_labor_treatment.value: Corporate & Union: * **PERMITTED** directly from general treasury funds, subject to standard individual contribution caps (\$39,200 Gov / \$5,900 Leg; Cal. Gov. Code § 85301).. Cash limit: * Maximum **\$100** cash contribution; anonymous contributions over \$100 strictly prohibited (\$0) (Cal. Gov. Code § 84300, 84304).. Prohibited sources: * Foreign nationals (Cal. Gov. Code § 85320); straw donors (Cal. Gov. Code § 84301); state contractors (Levine Act, Cal. Gov. Code § 84308: \$250 limit on appointed boards/commissions)..
corporate_labor_treatment.official_source: Political Reform Act of 1974 (PRA), Cal. Gov. Code § 81000 et seq.; 2 CCR § 18110 et seq.

public_financing.value: State public financing prohibited by PRA § 85300 (struck down for charter cities; San Francisco, Los Angeles, and Berkeley maintain municipal public matching systems).
public_financing.official_source: Political Reform Act of 1974 (PRA), Cal. Gov. Code § 81000 et seq.; 2 CCR § 18110 et seq.

independent_expenditures.value: Independent Expenditure PACs (Super PACs) file 24-hr Form 496 for expenditures ≥\$1,000 made within 90 days of election (Cal. Gov. Code § 84204). **California DISCLOSE Act:** Political ads must prominently display the **top 3 contributors of \$50,000+** (Cal. Gov. Code § 84501 et seq.).
independent_expenditures.official_source: Political Reform Act of 1974 (PRA), Cal. Gov. Code § 81000 et seq.; 2 CCR § 18110 et seq.

campaign_finance_enforcement_agency.value: Administered by Fair Political Practices Commission (FPPC). under Political Reform Act of 1974 (PRA), Cal. Gov. Code § 81000 et seq.; 2 CCR § 18110 et seq..
campaign_finance_enforcement_agency.official_source: Political Reform Act of 1974 (PRA), Cal. Gov. Code § 81000 et seq.; 2 CCR § 18110 et seq.

late_failure_consequences.value: Statutory late fees per day/filing; compliance audit; disqualification from ballot/certificate of election for failure to file; civil penalty enforcement; criminal referral for willful violations. Official sanctions: Civil fines up to $5,000 per violation, Misdemeanor referral, Restitution.
late_failure_consequences.official_source: Political Reform Act of 1974 (PRA), Cal. Gov. Code § 81000 et seq.; 2 CCR § 18110 et seq.

financial_disclosure.value: Form 700 (Statement of Economic Interests) filed by April 1. * Form 700 (Statement of Economic Interests) filed annually by April 1 covering investments, real property, and income (Cal. Gov. Code § 87200 et seq.).
financial_disclosure.official_source: Political Reform Act of 1974 (PRA), Cal. Gov. Code § 81000 et seq.; 2 CCR § 18110 et seq.

gift_restrictions.value: * General gift limit from non-lobbyists is **\$590 per calendar year** (2025–2026 indexed threshold; Cal. Gov. Code § 89503).
gift_restrictions.official_source: Political Reform Act of 1974 (PRA), Cal. Gov. Code § 81000 et seq.; 2 CCR § 18110 et seq.

conflicts_of_interest.value: * Mandatory disqualification/recusal on governmental decisions affecting personal financial interests by \$1,000+ (Cal. Gov. Code § 87100, 87103).
conflicts_of_interest.official_source: Political Reform Act of 1974 (PRA), Cal. Gov. Code § 81000 et seq.; 2 CCR § 18110 et seq.

recusal_disqualification.value: Mandatory recusal: public officials must disclose conflicts on the official record and disqualify/abstain from voting, deliberating, or exercising official discretionary authority on matter affecting pecuniary interests. * Mandatory disqualification/recusal on governmental decisions affecting personal financial interests by \$1,000+ (Cal. Gov. Code § 87100, 87103).
recusal_disqualification.official_source: Political Reform Act of 1974 (PRA), Cal. Gov. Code § 81000 et seq.; 2 CCR § 18110 et seq.

revolving_door_restrictions.value: * **1-year cooling-off period** prohibiting former legislators and state administrative officials from lobbying their former agency (Cal. Gov. Code § 87406); **permanent ban** on switching sides in judicial/quasi-judicial proceedings (Cal. Gov. Code § 87401).
revolving_door_restrictions.official_source: Political Reform Act of 1974 (PRA), Cal. Gov. Code § 81000 et seq.; 2 CCR § 18110 et seq.

ethics_enforcement_structure.value: Ethics oversight and enforcement vested in Fair Political Practices Commission (FPPC).. Authorized to investigate complaints, issue advisory opinions, conduct audits, issue subpoenas, levy civil fines, and refer criminal violations.
ethics_enforcement_structure.official_source: Political Reform Act of 1974 (PRA), Cal. Gov. Code § 81000 et seq.; 2 CCR § 18110 et seq.

lobbyist_registration_trigger.value: Regulated by FPPC / Secretary of State. Trigger: compensated lobbying. Quarterly reports due end of month following calendar quarter (Cal. Gov. Code § 86113). lobbyist_registration_trigger.official_source: Political Reform Act of 1974 (PRA), Cal. Gov. Code § 81000 et seq.; 2 CCR § 18110 et seq.

client_principal_relationship.value: Principals/clients employing lobbyists must file formal authorization/registration, certify expenditure reporting, and pay applicable principal fees alongside individual lobbyist registrations.
client_principal_relationship.official_source: Political Reform Act of 1974 (PRA), Cal. Gov. Code § 81000 et seq.; 2 CCR § 18110 et seq.

lobbying_reporting_scope_cadence.official_source: Political Reform Act of 1974 (PRA), Cal. Gov. Code § 81000 et seq.; 2 CCR § 18110 et seq.

lobbying_gift_restrictions.official_source: Political Reform Act of 1974 (PRA), Cal. Gov. Code § 81000 et seq.; 2 CCR § 18110 et seq.

lobbying_enforcement_body.official_source: Political Reform Act of 1974 (PRA), Cal. Gov. Code § 81000 et seq.; 2 CCR § 18110 et seq.

lobbying_structural_exceptions.official_source: Political Reform Act of 1974 (PRA), Cal. Gov. Code § 81000 et seq.; 2 CCR § 18110 et seq.

reporting_cadence_events.official_source: 15 Del. C. Chapter 80 (Campaign Financing and Disclosure Act); 29 Del. C. Chapter 58 (State Ethics Code).

contribution_limits.value: Individuals: * Statewide: **\$2,000** per election period; Non-Statewide (Legislative / Local): **\$1,000** per election period (15 Del. C. § 8010).. PACs/Parties: * PACs: \$2,000 statewide / \$1,000 legislative. Political party: \$20,000 (Governor) / \$5,000 (Senate) / \$3,000 (House) per election period (15 Del. C. § 8010)..
contribution_limits.official_source: 15 Del. C. Chapter 80 (Campaign Financing and Disclosure Act); 29 Del. C. Chapter 58 (State Ethics Code).

corporate_labor_treatment.value: Corporate & Union: * **PERMITTED** directly from treasury funds, subject to standard individual limits (\$2,000 statewide / \$1,000 legislative; 15 Del. C. § 8010).. Cash limit: * Maximum **\$50** cash contribution; anonymous contributions strictly banned (\$0) (15 Del. C. § 8016).. Prohibited sources: * Foreign nationals; straw donors (15 Del. C. § 8012)..
corporate_labor_treatment.official_source: 15 Del. C. Chapter 80 (Campaign Financing and Disclosure Act); 29 Del. C. Chapter 58 (State Ethics Code).

public_financing.official_source: 15 Del. C. Chapter 80 (Campaign Financing and Disclosure Act); 29 Del. C. Chapter 58 (State Ethics Code).

independent_expenditures.value: Independent expenditures >\$500 must file reports within 24 hours of expenditure (15 Del. C. § 8031). Clear attribution statement mandatory.
independent_expenditures.official_source: 15 Del. C. Chapter 80 (Campaign Financing and Disclosure Act); 29 Del. C. Chapter 58 (State Ethics Code).

campaign_finance_enforcement_agency.value: Administered by Delaware Department of Elections / State Public Integrity Commission (PIC). under 15 Del. C. Chapter 80 (Campaign Financing and Disclosure Act); 29 Del. C. Chapter 58 (State Ethics Code)..
campaign_finance_enforcement_agency.official_source: 15 Del. C. Chapter 80 (Campaign Financing and Disclosure Act); 29 Del. C. Chapter 58 (State Ethics Code).

late_failure_consequences.value: Statutory late fees per day/filing; compliance audit; disqualification from ballot/certificate of election for failure to file; civil penalty enforcement; criminal referral for willful violations. Official sanctions: Civil fines, Public reprimand, Misdemeanor referral.
late_failure_consequences.official_source: 15 Del. C. Chapter 80 (Campaign Financing and Disclosure Act); 29 Del. C. Chapter 58 (State Ethics Code).

financial_disclosure.value: Financial Disclosure Report filed by March 15. * Annual financial disclosure filed by March 15 (29 Del. C. § 5812).
financial_disclosure.official_source: 15 Del. C. Chapter 80 (Campaign Financing and Disclosure Act); 29 Del. C. Chapter 58 (State Ethics Code).

gift_restrictions.value: * Public officers may not accept gifts of substantial value; nominal gifts (<\$50) permitted if not given to influence official duties (29 Del. C. § 5806).
gift_restrictions.official_source: 15 Del. C. Chapter 80 (Campaign Financing and Disclosure Act); 29 Del. C. Chapter 58 (State Ethics Code).

conflicts_of_interest.value: * Mandatory recusal on matters of direct personal financial benefit (29 Del. C. § 5805).
conflicts_of_interest.official_source: 15 Del. C. Chapter 80 (Campaign Financing and Disclosure Act); 29 Del. C. Chapter 58 (State Ethics Code).

recusal_disqualification.value: Mandatory recusal: public officials must disclose conflicts on the official record and disqualify/abstain from voting, deliberating, or exercising official discretionary authority on matter affecting pecuniary interests. * Mandatory recusal on matters of direct personal financial benefit (29 Del. C. § 5805).
recusal_disqualification.official_source: 15 Del. C. Chapter 80 (Campaign Financing and Disclosure Act); 29 Del. C. Chapter 58 (State Ethics Code).

revolving_door_restrictions.value: * **2-year cooling-off period** for former state employees/officials from representing clients before former agency (29 Del. C. § 5805(d)).
revolving_door_restrictions.official_source: 15 Del. C. Chapter 80 (Campaign Financing and Disclosure Act); 29 Del. C. Chapter 58 (State Ethics Code).

ethics_enforcement_structure.value: Ethics oversight and enforcement vested in Delaware Department of Elections / State Public Integrity Commission (PIC).. Authorized to investigate complaints, issue advisory opinions, conduct audits, issue subpoenas, levy civil fines, and refer criminal violations.
ethics_enforcement_structure.official_source: 15 Del. C. Chapter 80 (Campaign Financing and Disclosure Act); 29 Del. C. Chapter 58 (State Ethics Code).

lobbyist_registration_trigger.value: Regulated by State Public Integrity Commission. Quarterly reports due 20th of month following quarter (29 Del. C. § 5831 et seq.).
lobbyist_registration_trigger.official_source: 15 Del. C. Chapter 80 (Campaign Financing and Disclosure Act); 29 Del. C. Chapter 58 (State Ethics Code).

client_principal_relationship.value: Principals/clients employing lobbyists must file formal authorization/registration, certify expenditure reporting, and pay applicable principal fees alongside individual lobbyist registrations.
client_principal_relationship.official_source: 15 Del. C. Chapter 80 (Campaign Financing and Disclosure Act); 29 Del. C. Chapter 58 (State Ethics Code).

lobbying_reporting_scope_cadence.value: Reporting cadence: quarterly. Discloses all lobbying compensation, itemized expenses for meals, entertainment, travel, gifts, advertising, and specific legislative/administrative bill or issue tracking.
lobbying_reporting_scope_cadence.official_source: 15 Del. C. Chapter 80 (Campaign Financing and Disclosure Act); 29 Del. C. Chapter 58 (State Ethics Code).

lobbying_gift_restrictions.value: Lobbyist gift rule: Nominal (<$50). Prohibits gifts, gratuities, entertainment, or meals from registered lobbyists/principals exceeding statutory cap. Sessional fundraising bans apply in applicable legislative cycles.
lobbying_gift_restrictions.official_source: 15 Del. C. Chapter 80 (Campaign Financing and Disclosure Act); 29 Del. C. Chapter 58 (State Ethics Code).

lobbying_enforcement_body.value: Lobbyist registry and compliance enforcement administered by Delaware Department of Elections / State Public Integrity Commission (PIC)..
lobbying_enforcement_body.official_source: 15 Del. C. Chapter 80 (Campaign Financing and Disclosure Act); 29 Del. C. Chapter 58 (State Ethics Code).

lobbying_structural_exceptions.value: Statutory exceptions: private citizens expressing personal opinions without compensation, public employees acting in official capacity, news media in regular dissemination of news/editorial, and invited expert witnesses giving formal legislative testimony.
lobbying_structural_exceptions.official_source: 15 Del. C. Chapter 80 (Campaign Financing and Disclosure Act); 29 Del. C. Chapter 58 (State Ethics Code).

us-fl.name: FLORIDA
us-fl.regulatory_agencies: Florida Commission on Ethics / Florida Elections Commission (FEC) / Division of Elections.
us-fl.primary_statutes: Fla. Stat. Chapter 106 (Campaign Financing); Chapter 112, Part III (Code of Ethics for Public Officers).

candidate_committee_registration.value: * Candidate must file Form DS-DE 9 (Appointment of Campaign Treasurer and Designation of Campaign Depository) *before* accepting any contribution or spending any fund ($0 threshold; Fla. Stat. § 106.021).. * Mandatory treasurer; candidate may act as treasurer. Mandatory designated depository in a financial institution authorized to do business in Florida (Fla. Stat. § 106.021).. * Single authorized campaign account per office sought..
candidate_committee_registration.official_source: Fla. Stat. Chapter 106 (Campaign Financing); Chapter 112, Part III (Code of Ethics for Public Officers).

reporting_cadence_events.value: * Monthly filings, shifting to bi-weekly and weekly filings in the 60 days before general election; daily 24-hr reports during the final week before election (Fla. Stat. § 106.07).
reporting_cadence_events.official_source: Fla. Stat. Chapter 106 (Campaign Financing); Chapter 112, Part III (Code of Ethics for Public Officers).

contribution_limits.value: Individuals: *. PACs/Parties: * Political PACs to Candidate: standard individual limits (\$3,000 statewide / \$1,000 leg). Political Parties to Candidate: \$250,000 (Governor) / \$50,000 (Legislative) per election (Fla. Stat. § 106.08)..
contribution_limits.official_source: Fla. Stat. Chapter 106 (Campaign Financing); Chapter 112, Part III (Code of Ethics for Public Officers).

corporate_labor_treatment.value: Corporate & Union: * **PERMITTED** directly from corporate/union treasury funds, subject to standard individual limits (\$3,000 statewide / \$1,000 leg; Fla. Stat. § 106.08).. Cash limit: * Maximum **\$50** cash contribution; anonymous contributions strictly prohibited (\$0) (Fla. Stat. § 106.09).. Prohibited sources: * Foreign nationals; straw donors; regulated utilities and gaming entities under certain specific statutory provisions..
corporate_labor_treatment.official_source: Fla. Stat. Chapter 106 (Campaign Financing); Chapter 112, Part III (Code of Ethics for Public Officers).

public_financing.value: **ACTIVE STATEWIDE GUBERNATORIAL & CABINET MATCHING PROGRAM** (Florida Election Campaign Financing Act, Fla. Stat. § 106.30–106.36). 2-to-1 public match on small-dollar donations up to \$250 for qualifying candidates who agree to voluntary expenditure limits.
public_financing.official_source: Fla. Stat. Chapter 106 (Campaign Financing); Chapter 112, Part III (Code of Ethics for Public Officers).

independent_expenditures.value: Political Committees making independent expenditures report on regular schedules, plus 24-hr reporting during the final 10 days before an election (Fla. Stat. § 106.071). Mandatory political disclaimer: "Paid political advertisement paid for by [Name, Address] independently of any candidate".
independent_expenditures.official_source: Fla. Stat. Chapter 106 (Campaign Financing); Chapter 112, Part III (Code of Ethics for Public Officers).

campaign_finance_enforcement_agency.value: Administered by Florida Commission on Ethics / Florida Elections Commission (FEC) / Division of Elections. under Fla. Stat. Chapter 106 (Campaign Financing); Chapter 112, Part III (Code of Ethics for Public Officers)..
campaign_finance_enforcement_agency.official_source: Fla. Stat. Chapter 106 (Campaign Financing); Chapter 112, Part III (Code of Ethics for Public Officers).

late_failure_consequences.value: Statutory late fees per day/filing; compliance audit; disqualification from ballot/certificate of election for failure to file; civil penalty enforcement; criminal referral for willful violations. Official sanctions: Civil fines up to $10,000, Removal from office, Impeachment referral.
late_failure_consequences.official_source: Fla. Stat. Chapter 106 (Campaign Financing); Chapter 112, Part III (Code of Ethics for Public Officers).

financial_disclosure.value: Form 6 (Full and Public Disclosure of Financial Interests) filed by July 1. * Form 6 (Full and Public Disclosure of Financial Interests) filed annually by July 1 disclosing net worth, all assets, and liabilities >\$1,000 (Fla. Const. art. II, § 8; Fla. Stat. § 112.3144).
financial_disclosure.official_source: Fla. Stat. Chapter 106 (Campaign Financing); Chapter 112, Part III (Code of Ethics for Public Officers).

gift_restrictions.value: * **STRICT ZERO-GIFT BAN**; reporting individuals and state legislators may not solicit or accept any gift, meal, beverage, or entertainment of any value from a registered lobbyist or principal (Fla. Stat. § 112.3148).
gift_restrictions.official_source: Fla. Stat. Chapter 106 (Campaign Financing); Chapter 112, Part III (Code of Ethics for Public Officers).

conflicts_of_interest.value: * Voting conflict requires public declaration and Form 8A/8B disclosure; recusal mandatory for local officials, declaration on floor for state legislators (Fla. Stat. § 112.3143).
conflicts_of_interest.official_source: Fla. Stat. Chapter 106 (Campaign Financing); Chapter 112, Part III (Code of Ethics for Public Officers).

recusal_disqualification.value: Mandatory recusal: public officials must disclose conflicts on the official record and disqualify/abstain from voting, deliberating, or exercising official discretionary authority on matter affecting pecuniary interests. * Voting conflict requires public declaration and Form 8A/8B disclosure; recusal mandatory for local officials, declaration on floor for state legislators (Fla. Stat. § 112.3143).
recusal_disqualification.official_source: Fla. Stat. Chapter 106 (Campaign Financing); Chapter 112, Part III (Code of Ethics for Public Officers).

revolving_door_restrictions.value: * **6-YEAR COOLING-OFF PERIOD** (Constitutional Amendment 12, effective 2022). Former legislators and statewide elected officers are barred for **6 full years** from lobbying the legislature or state agencies for compensation (Fla. Const. art. II, § 8(f)).
revolving_door_restrictions.official_source: Fla. Stat. Chapter 106 (Campaign Financing); Chapter 112, Part III (Code of Ethics for Public Officers).

ethics_enforcement_structure.value: Ethics oversight and enforcement vested in Florida Commission on Ethics / Florida Elections Commission (FEC) / Division of Elections.. Authorized to investigate complaints, issue advisory opinions, conduct audits, issue subpoenas, levy civil fines, and refer criminal violations.
ethics_enforcement_structure.official_source: Fla. Stat. Chapter 106 (Campaign Financing); Chapter 112, Part III (Code of Ethics for Public Officers).

lobbyist_registration_trigger.value: Regulated by Florida Commission on Ethics / Legislative Lobbyist Registration. Semi-annual expenditure reporting due May 15 and November 15 (Fla. Stat. § 11.045, 112.3215).
lobbyist_registration_trigger.official_source: Fla. Stat. Chapter 106 (Campaign Financing); Chapter 112, Part III (Code of Ethics for Public Officers).

client_principal_relationship.value: Principals/clients employing lobbyists must file formal authorization/registration, certify expenditure reporting, and pay applicable principal fees alongside individual lobbyist registrations.
client_principal_relationship.official_source: Fla. Stat. Chapter 106 (Campaign Financing); Chapter 112, Part III (Code of Ethics for Public Officers).

lobbying_reporting_scope_cadence.value: Reporting cadence: semi_annual. Discloses all lobbying compensation, itemized expenses for meals, entertainment, travel, gifts, advertising, and specific legislative/administrative bill or issue tracking.
lobbying_reporting_scope_cadence.official_source: Fla. Stat. Chapter 106 (Campaign Financing); Chapter 112, Part III (Code of Ethics for Public Officers).

lobbying_gift_restrictions.value: Lobbyist gift rule: $0 (Strict lobbyist gift ban). Prohibits gifts, gratuities, entertainment, or meals from registered lobbyists/principals exceeding statutory cap. Sessional fundraising bans apply in applicable legislative cycles.
lobbying_gift_restrictions.official_source: Fla. Stat. Chapter 106 (Campaign Financing); Chapter 112, Part III (Code of Ethics for Public Officers).

lobbying_enforcement_body.value: Lobbyist registry and compliance enforcement administered by Florida Commission on Ethics / Florida Elections Commission (FEC) / Division of Elections..
lobbying_enforcement_body.official_source: Fla. Stat. Chapter 106 (Campaign Financing); Chapter 112, Part III (Code of Ethics for Public Officers).

lobbying_structural_exceptions.value: Statutory exceptions: private citizens expressing personal opinions without compensation, public employees acting in official capacity, news media in regular dissemination of news/editorial, and invited expert witnesses giving formal legislative testimony.
lobbying_structural_exceptions.official_source: Fla. Stat. Chapter 106 (Campaign Financing); Chapter 112, Part III (Code of Ethics for Public Officers).

corporate_labor_treatment.value: Corporate & Union: * **PERMITTED** directly from treasury funds, subject to standard limits (\$8,400 statewide / \$3,300 leg; O.C.G.A. § 21-5-41).. late_failure_consequences.official_source: Georgia Code (O.C.G.A.) Title 21, Chapter 5 (Ethics in Government Act).

financial_disclosure.official_source: Georgia Code (O.C.G.A.) Title 21, Chapter 5 (Ethics in Government Act).

us-ky.primary_statutes: KRS Chapter 121 (Campaign Finance); KRS Chapter 6 (Legislative Ethics); KRS Chapter 11A (Executive Ethics).

candidate_committee_registration.value: * Candidate must file Form KREF-001 (Appointment of Campaign Treasurer and Depository) before receiving or spending any money ($0 trigger; KRS 121.160).. * Mandatory treasurer; candidate may act as treasurer; mandatory Kentucky bank depository (KRS 121.160).. * Single candidate committee per office sought..
candidate_committee_registration.official_source: KRS Chapter 121 (Campaign Finance); KRS Chapter 6 (Legislative Ethics); KRS Chapter 11A (Executive Ethics).

reporting_cadence_events.official_source: KRS Chapter 121 (Campaign Finance); KRS Chapter 6 (Legislative Ethics); KRS Chapter 11A (Executive Ethics).

contribution_limits.value: Individuals: * **\$3,500** per election (Primary and General separate = \$7,000 total cycle; indexed to FEC limit under HB 139) for all statewide, legislative, and local candidates.. PACs/Parties: * PACs to Candidate: **\$3,500** per election. State Executive Party & Caucus Committees: \$10,000/year from individuals (KRS 121.150(11))..
contribution_limits.official_source: KRS Chapter 121 (Campaign Finance); KRS Chapter 6 (Legislative Ethics); KRS Chapter 11A (Executive Ethics).

corporate_labor_treatment.value: Corporate & Union: See statutory schedule. Cash limit: * Maximum **\$100** cash contribution; anonymous contributions strictly banned (\$0) and escheat to state general fund (KRS 121.150).. Prohibited sources: * Corporations; foreign nationals; straw donors; state contractors subject to pay-to-play restrictions. Sessional lobbyist ban: lawmakers cannot accept campaign contributions from lobbyists during General Assembly sessions (KRS 6.767)..
corporate_labor_treatment.official_source: KRS Chapter 121 (Campaign Finance); KRS Chapter 6 (Legislative Ethics); KRS Chapter 11A (Executive Ethics).

public_financing.value: Not Applicable (`not-applicable`; former gubernatorial matching fund repealed).
public_financing.official_source: KRS Chapter 121 (Campaign Finance); KRS Chapter 6 (Legislative Ethics); KRS Chapter 11A (Executive Ethics).

independent_expenditures.value: Independent expenditure committees register and file reports under KRS 121.180. Paid-for attribution mandatory on all political advertising (KRS 121.190).
independent_expenditures.official_source: KRS Chapter 121 (Campaign Finance); KRS Chapter 6 (Legislative Ethics); KRS Chapter 11A (Executive Ethics).

campaign_finance_enforcement_agency.value: Administered by Kentucky Registry of Election Finance (KREF) / Kentucky Legislative Ethics Commission (KLEC) / Executive Branch Ethics Commission (EBEC). under KRS Chapter 121 (Campaign Finance); KRS Chapter 6 (Legislative Ethics); KRS Chapter 11A (Executive Ethics)..
campaign_finance_enforcement_agency.official_source: KRS Chapter 121 (Campaign Finance); KRS Chapter 6 (Legislative Ethics); KRS Chapter 11A (Executive Ethics).

late_failure_consequences.value: Statutory late fees per day/filing; compliance audit; disqualification from ballot/certificate of election for failure to file; civil penalty enforcement; criminal referral for willful violations. Official sanctions: Civil fines up to $5,000, Class D felony prosecution, Censure/removal.
late_failure_consequences.official_source: KRS Chapter 121 (Campaign Finance); KRS Chapter 6 (Legislative Ethics); KRS Chapter 11A (Executive Ethics).

financial_disclosure.value: Statement of Financial Interests filed by February 15 (Leg) / April 15 (Exec). * Statement of Financial Interests filed annually by February 15 (legislative, KRS 6.781) and April 15 (executive, KRS 11A.050).
financial_disclosure.official_source: KRS Chapter 121 (Campaign Finance); KRS Chapter 6 (Legislative Ethics); KRS Chapter 11A (Executive Ethics).

gift_restrictions.value: * **STRICT ZERO-GIFT BAN**; legislative code strictly prohibits legislators from accepting gifts, meals, or hospitality from registered lobbyists (KRS 6.751). Executive branch: nominal gift ban under KRS 11A.045.
gift_restrictions.official_source: KRS Chapter 121 (Campaign Finance); KRS Chapter 6 (Legislative Ethics); KRS Chapter 11A (Executive Ethics).

conflicts_of_interest.value: * Mandatory disclosure and abstention from voting on matters of personal pecuniary gain (KRS 6.761; KRS 11A.030).
conflicts_of_interest.official_source: KRS Chapter 121 (Campaign Finance); KRS Chapter 6 (Legislative Ethics); KRS Chapter 11A (Executive Ethics).

recusal_disqualification.value: Mandatory recusal: public officials must disclose conflicts on the official record and disqualify/abstain from voting, deliberating, or exercising official discretionary authority on matter affecting pecuniary interests. * Mandatory disclosure and abstention from voting on matters of personal pecuniary gain (KRS 6.761; KRS 11A.030).
recusal_disqualification.official_source: KRS Chapter 121 (Campaign Finance); KRS Chapter 6 (Legislative Ethics); KRS Chapter 11A (Executive Ethics).

revolving_door_restrictions.value: * **2-YEAR COOLING-OFF PERIOD**; enacted via 2026 Ky. Acts ch. 175 (HB 139, eff. July 15, 2026), expanding the former 1-year ban to **2 full years** prohibiting former legislators from lobbying the General Assembly (KRS 6.757). Executive officials subject to 1-year agency lobbying ban and permanent matter bar (KRS 11A.040).
revolving_door_restrictions.official_source: KRS Chapter 121 (Campaign Finance); KRS Chapter 6 (Legislative Ethics); KRS Chapter 11A (Executive Ethics).

ethics_enforcement_structure.value: Ethics oversight and enforcement vested in Kentucky Registry of Election Finance (KREF) / Kentucky Legislative Ethics Commission (KLEC) / Executive Branch Ethics Commission (EBEC).. Authorized to investigate complaints, issue advisory opinions, conduct audits, issue subpoenas, levy civil fines, and refer criminal violations.
ethics_enforcement_structure.official_source: KRS Chapter 121 (Campaign Finance); KRS Chapter 6 (Legislative Ethics); KRS Chapter 11A (Executive Ethics).

lobbyist_registration_trigger.value: Legislative lobbying regulated by KLEC (KRS 6.801–6.829); Executive lobbying regulated by EBEC (KRS 11A.201–11A.246). Updated registration statements due every 2 years; expenditure filings due semi-annually and during sessions.
lobbyist_registration_trigger.official_source: KRS Chapter 121 (Campaign Finance); KRS Chapter 6 (Legislative Ethics); KRS Chapter 11A (Executive Ethics).

client_principal_relationship.value: Principals/clients employing lobbyists must file formal authorization/registration, certify expenditure reporting, and pay applicable principal fees alongside individual lobbyist registrations.
client_principal_relationship.official_source: KRS Chapter 121 (Campaign Finance); KRS Chapter 6 (Legislative Ethics); KRS Chapter 11A (Executive Ethics).

lobbying_reporting_scope_cadence.value: Reporting cadence: periodic_and_session. Discloses all lobbying compensation, itemized expenses for meals, entertainment, travel, gifts, advertising, and specific legislative/administrative bill or issue tracking.
lobbying_reporting_scope_cadence.official_source: KRS Chapter 121 (Campaign Finance); KRS Chapter 6 (Legislative Ethics); KRS Chapter 11A (Executive Ethics).

lobbying_gift_restrictions.value: Lobbyist gift rule: $0 (Strict zero-gift ban to legislators). Prohibits gifts, gratuities, entertainment, or meals from registered lobbyists/principals exceeding statutory cap. Sessional fundraising bans apply in applicable legislative cycles.
lobbying_gift_restrictions.official_source: KRS Chapter 121 (Campaign Finance); KRS Chapter 6 (Legislative Ethics); KRS Chapter 11A (Executive Ethics).

lobbying_enforcement_body.value: Lobbyist registry and compliance enforcement administered by Kentucky Registry of Election Finance (KREF) / Kentucky Legislative Ethics Commission (KLEC) / Executive Branch Ethics Commission (EBEC)..
lobbying_enforcement_body.official_source: KRS Chapter 121 (Campaign Finance); KRS Chapter 6 (Legislative Ethics); KRS Chapter 11A (Executive Ethics).

lobbying_structural_exceptions.value: Statutory exceptions: private citizens expressing personal opinions without compensation, public employees acting in official capacity, news media in regular dissemination of news/editorial, and invited expert witnesses giving formal legislative testimony.
lobbying_structural_exceptions.official_source: KRS Chapter 121 (Campaign Finance); KRS Chapter 6 (Legislative Ethics); KRS Chapter 11A (Executive Ethics).

lobbying_gift_restrictions.official_source: Wis. Stat. Chapter 11 (Campaign Financing); Chapter 13, Subchapter III (Lobbying); Chapter 19, Subchapter III (Code of Ethics).

lobbying_enforcement_body.value: Lobbyist registry and compliance enforcement administered by Wisconsin Elections Commission (WEC) / Wisconsin Ethics Commission..
lobbying_enforcement_body.official_source: Wis. Stat. Chapter 11 (Campaign Financing); Chapter 13, Subchapter III (Lobbying); Chapter 19, Subchapter III (Code of Ethics).

lobbying_structural_exceptions.value: Statutory exceptions: private citizens expressing personal opinions without compensation, public employees acting in official capacity, news media in regular dissemination of news/editorial, and invited expert witnesses giving formal legislative testimony.
lobbying_structural_exceptions.official_source: Wis. Stat. Chapter 11 (Campaign Financing); Chapter 13, Subchapter III (Lobbying); Chapter 19, Subchapter III (Code of Ethics).

us-fed.name: United States (Federal Baseline)
us-fed.regulatory_agencies: Federal Election Commission (FEC) / U.S. Office of Government Ethics (OGE) / House Ethics / Senate Ethics / DOJ Public Integrity
us-fed.primary_statutes: Federal Election Campaign Act (52 U.S.C. § 30101 et seq.); Ethics in Government Act (5 U.S.C. app. § 101 et seq.); 18 U.S.C. §§ 201-209; Lobbying Disclosure Act (2 U.S.C. § 1601 et seq.)

candidate_committee_registration.value: Statement of Candidacy (FEC Form 2) within 15 days of qualifying as candidate ($5,000 raised or spent threshold). Statement of Organization (FEC Form 1) for Principal Campaign Committee (PCC) within 10 days of designation. Single authorized PCC per candidate per federal election cycle (52 U.S.C. § 30102(e)). Dedicated campaign depository bank account mandatory.

reporting_cadence_events.value: Quarterly reporting (April 15, July 15, October 15, January 31); Pre-Primary (12-day); Pre-General (12-day); Post-General (30-day). 48-Hour Notice (Form 6) mandatory for contributions of $1,000+ received within 20 days but more than 48 hours before election day (52 U.S.C. § 30104(a)(6)).

contribution_limits.value: 2025–2026 Biennial Cycle (indexed to inflation): Individuals to Candidate: $3,500 per election (Primary / General separate). Individuals to National Party Committees: $44,300 per calendar year. Multicandidate PAC to Candidate: $5,000 per election. Candidate self-funding: unlimited under Buckley v. Valeo; post-FEC v. Ted Cruz for Senate (2022), the 52 U.S.C. § 30116(j) $250k personal loan repayment cap is invalid.
contribution_limits.official_source: 52 U.S.C. § 30116; 11 C.F.R. § 110.1; FEC v. Ted Cruz for Senate, 596 U.S. 289 (2022)

corporate_labor_treatment.value: Direct contributions from corporate or labor union general treasury funds strictly PROHIBITED ($0). Permitted solely through Separate Segregated Funds (SSFs / PACs) funded by voluntary contributions from connected executive/shareholder or union member classes. Cash contribution maximum: $100. Anonymous contributions banned ($0). Federal contractor contributions strictly banned (52 U.S.C. § 30119). Foreign nationals banned (52 U.S.C. § 30121).

public_financing.value: Presidential Election Campaign Fund (26 U.S.C. § 9001 et seq.) provides voluntary matching funds for primaries and lump-sum grants for general presidential campaigns (funded by voluntary $3 tax checkoff), subject to mandatory spending limits; effectively obsolete for major party nominees since 2008 due to private fundraising scale. Congressional public financing: NOT_APPLICABLE ($0 / none).

independent_expenditures.value: Independent Expenditure-Only Committees (Super PACs) authorized post-SpeechNow.org v. FEC (2010); unlimited contributions from individuals, corporations, and unions. Pre-election flash reporting: 48-Hour Report for aggregate IEs >= $10,000 outside 20-day window; 24-Hour Report for aggregate IEs >= $1,000 received/spent within 20 days of election. Stand By Your Ad disclaimers mandatory on broadcast, print, and digital media (52 U.S.C. § 30120).

campaign_finance_enforcement_agency.value: Federal Election Commission (FEC): 6 commissioners appointed by President and confirmed by Senate; statutory partisan balance rule: no more than 3 commissioners from same political party; affirmative vote of 4 commissioners required to initiate investigations, approve advisory opinions, find reason to believe, or settle civil enforcement matters.

late_failure_consequences.value: Formulaic civil money penalties under FEC Administrative Fine Program calculated based on report lateness and receipts/disbursements; civil enforcement lawsuits in U.S. District Court seeking injunctive relief and civil penalties up to greater of $10,000 or contribution/expenditure amount (or $25,000 for knowing and willful); mandatory referrals to Department of Justice (Public Integrity Section) for knowing and willful criminal violations.
late_failure_consequences.official_source: 52 U.S.C. § 30109; 11 C.F.R. Part 111, Subpart B

financial_disclosure.value: Mandatory annual Public Financial Disclosure Reports (OGE Form 278e for Executive Branch; House Form A/B; Senate Form 278) filed by May 15 covering earned and unearned income (> $200), assets and property interests (> $1,000), liabilities (> $10,000), positions held outside government, and agreement/arrangements. Periodic Transaction Reports (OGE Form 278-T / STOCK Act) required within 30-45 days of any securities transaction exceeding $1,000.
financial_disclosure.official_source: 5 U.S.C. app. §§ 101-111; 5 C.F.R. Part 2634; STOCK Act, Pub. L. 112-105

gift_restrictions.value: Executive Branch: 5 C.F.R. § 2635.202 prohibits soliciting or accepting gifts from prohibited sources (contractors, regulated entities, lobbyists) or given because of official position; exception for gifts valued at $20 or less per occasion, not to exceed $50 aggregate from single source per calendar year. Legislative Branch: House Rule 25 / Senate Rule 35 caps gifts at under $50 per occasion, < $100 annual aggregate from any single source; gifts of any value from registered lobbyists strictly banned.
gift_restrictions.official_source: 5 U.S.C. § 7353; 5 C.F.R. § 2635.201 et seq.; House Rule 25; Senate Rule 35

conflicts_of_interest.value: Executive Branch: 18 U.S.C. § 208 criminalizes personal and substantial participation in any judicial proceeding, application, contract, claim, or particular matter in which the employee, spouse, minor child, general partner, or prospective employer has a financial interest. President and Vice President are statutorily exempt from 18 U.S.C. § 208 by definition of 'officer/employee' under 18 U.S.C. § 202, but subject to financial disclosure and Constitution's Foreign/Domestic Emoluments Clauses.
conflicts_of_interest.official_source: 18 U.S.C. §§ 202, 208; 5 C.F.R. Part 2635, Subpart D; U.S. Const. art. I, § 9, cl. 8; art. II, § 1, cl. 7

recusal_disqualification.value: Mandatory disqualification/recusal from official actions where personal pecuniary interest exists unless statutory 18 U.S.C. § 208(b)(1) written waiver is granted in advance by appointing authority determining interest is not substantial. Legislative Branch: House Rule 3, clause 1 provides members shall not vote on question where they have direct personal or pecuniary interest (traditionally left to individual member conscience).

revolving_door_restrictions.value: 18 U.S.C. § 207 post-employment restrictions: Lifetime ban on switching sides and representing clients on particular matters involving specific parties personally and substantially handled while in government. 2-Year ban on matters under official responsibility within 1 year before leaving. 1-Year cooling-off period for Senior Executive personnel and Members of House representing or lobbying their former agency or Congress. 2-Year cooling-off period for U.S. Senators (Senate Rule 33.9). 1-Year ban on representing foreign governments/parties for very senior officials.
revolving_door_restrictions.official_source: 18 U.S.C. § 207; 5 C.F.R. Part 2641; House Rule 25; Senate Rule 33.9

ethics_enforcement_structure.value: U.S. Office of Government Ethics (OGE) provides executive branch ethics policy, program review, and financial disclosure certification. Criminal conflict-of-interest enforcement by DOJ Public Integrity Section and U.S. Attorneys. Congressional ethics enforcement: House Committee on Ethics (bipartisan 5R/5D) assisted by independent nonpartisan Office of Congressional Ethics (OCE); Senate Select Committee on Ethics (bipartisan 3R/3D).

lobbyist_registration_trigger.value: Lobbying Disclosure Act (LDA) of 1995: individual must register as a lobbyist if: (1) employed or retained for compensation; (2) makes more than one lobbying contact; and (3) spends 20% or more of overall time on lobbying activities on behalf of that client during a quarterly period. Registration threshold: lobbying firm income from client exceeds $3,000/quarter, or organization in-house lobbying expenses exceed $14,000/quarter (adjusted for inflation). Form LD-1 filed within 45 days of first contact or employment.
lobbyist_registration_trigger.official_source: 2 U.S.C. §§ 1602, 1603; LDA Guidance (Clerk of House & Secretary of Senate)

client_principal_relationship.value: Lobbying firm must register separately for each retained client (Form LD-1). In-house lobbying organizations register the organization itself and list individual in-house employee lobbyists. Registrations require disclosure of client identity, general business, foreign entity ownership interest (> 20%), and individual lobbyists authorized to act.

lobbying_reporting_scope_cadence.value: Quarterly Activity Reports (Form LD-2) filed by April 20, July 20, October 20, January 20 disclosing total lobbying income or expenses (rounded to nearest $10,000), specific bill numbers, executive branch agencies and houses of Congress contacted, and issue areas. Semi-Annual Contribution Reports (Form LD-203) filed by July 30 and January 30 disclosing federal PAC/campaign contributions, honorary contributions, and certifications of gift rule compliance.

lobbying_gift_restrictions.value: Honest Leadership and Open Government Act (HLOGA) of 2007: registered lobbyists, lobbying firms, and organizations employing lobbyists are prohibited from providing gifts, travel, or lodging to covered legislative or executive officials with knowledge that acceptance violates congressional or executive gift rules. Form LD-203 requires affirmative certification of full compliance with House and Senate gift rules under penalty of perjury (2 U.S.C. § 1604(e)).

lobbying_enforcement_body.value: Administered jointly by the Clerk of the House (Legislative Resource Center) and the Secretary of the Senate (Office of Public Records). Authority to review filings, issue non-compliance notices, and refer unresolved violations to the U.S. Attorney for the District of Columbia for civil enforcement and criminal prosecution.

lobbying_structural_exceptions.value: Statutory exceptions to 'lobbying contact': communications made by public officials acting in official capacity; media organizations; speeches or publications made through mass communications; formal participation in public agency rulemaking hearings or on-the-record administrative adjudications; written responses to oral or written agency inquiries; testimony given before a congressional committee; and grassroots communications encouraging the public to contact officials.
